</style>

The bezel is the only one, and it is DRAWN BY DEFAULT AND TAKEN OFF IN THE VIEWER - which is a reversal, and the reason is worth keeping. It was `optional: bezel` before, meaning the build dropped it unless asked for it by name. The argument was that it hides the drives it protects, so the default drawing should leave it off. That is a fair thing to want and it was the wrong mechanism for it: `optional` excludes a part from the ARTIFACT, so nothing downstream could put it back. A machine that ships with a bezel rendered as one that has none, in every consumer, with no way to ask. The kit already had the right control. `behaviour: mounts` puts a pull handle on any cover - "take off this cover to see behind it" - and it drives 2D and 3D alike.   <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='dell/psu-1100w-ac-14g@'] .state-fault { --led-color: #eab308; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/psu-1100w-ac-14g@'] .state-fault { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    @keyframes portrayal-seq-dell-psu-1100w-ac-14g-mismatch {
      0%, 3.9% { opacity: 1; fill: #22c55e; }
      4%, 7.9% { opacity: 0; }
      8%, 11.9% { opacity: 1; fill: #22c55e; }
      12%, 15.9% { opacity: 0; }
      16%, 19.9% { opacity: 1; fill: #22c55e; }
      20%, 23.9% { opacity: 0; }
      24%, 27.9% { opacity: 1; fill: #22c55e; }
      28%, 31.9% { opacity: 0; }
      32%, 35.9% { opacity: 1; fill: #22c55e; }
      36%, 99.9% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    g[data-ref^='dell/psu-1100w-ac-14g@'] .state-mismatch { animation: portrayal-seq-dell-psu-1100w-ac-14g-mismatch 3.125s steps(1, end) infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/psu-1100w-ac-14g@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/psu-1100w-ac-14g@'] .state-updating { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/psu-1100w-ac-14g@'] .state-updating { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/rj45-port-14g@'] .state-active { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/rj45-port-14g@'] .state-active { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/rj45-port-14g@'] .state-degraded { --led-color: #eab308; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/rj45-port-14g@'] .state-identify { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/rj45-port-14g@'] .state-identify { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/rj45-port-14g@'] .state-up { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/system-id-button-14g@'] .state-identify { --led-color: #2563eb; }

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    @keyframes portrayal-seq-dell-control-panel-left-14g-disabled {
      0%, 3.25196% { opacity: 1; fill: #f8fafc; }
      3.35196%, 6.60391% { opacity: 0; }

      30.1676%, 99.9% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-disabled { animation: portrayal-seq-dell-control-panel-left-14g-disabled 3.58s steps(1, end) infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-fail-safe { --led-color: #eab308; }

    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-fault { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }

    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-identify { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-ready { --led-color: #f8fafc; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-transfer { --led-color: #f8fafc; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-transfer { animation: portrayal-blink 0.25s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-unresponsive { --led-color: #eab308; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-unresponsive { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-updating { --led-color: #f8fafc; }
    g[data-ref^='dell/control-panel-left-14g@'] .state-updating { animation: portrayal-blink 2s linear infinite; }

</style>

  <g id="bezel" data-path="bezel" data-class="bezel" data-behaviour="mounts" data-ref="dell/bezel-2u-14g@1:2.2.1" data-body-depth="23.3" data-rel-pos="0" transform="translate(24.3,2.23)" data-group="covers" data-group-role="service" data-description="removable covers over the face. The bezel is the only one, and it is DRAWN BY DEFAULT AND TAKEN OFF IN THE VIEWER - which is a reversal, and the reason is worth keeping. It was `optional: bezel` before, meaning the build dropped it unless asked for it by name. The argument was that it hides the drives it protects, so the default drawing should leave it off. That is a fair thing to want and it was the wrong mechanism for it: `optional` excludes a part from the ARTIFACT, so nothing downstream could put it back. A machine that ships with a bezel rendered as one that has none, in every consumer, with no way to ask. The kit already had the right control. `behaviour: mounts` puts a pull handle on any cover - "take off this cover to see behind it" - and it drives 2D and 3D alike. So the bezel is placed like any other part and the drives are one click away, which is the same gesture the top panel uses and one fewer concept than it had." data-for="drive-0 drive-1 drive-2 drive-3 drive-4 drive-5 drive-6 drive-7 drive-8 drive-9 drive-10 drive-11 drive-12 drive-13 drive-14 drive-15 drive-16 drive-17 drive-18 drive-19 drive-20 drive-21 drive-22 drive-23 panel-left">
